explanation: Henry Ford argued that workers with free Saturdays would have more time to buy and enjoy goods, cars included. He had already doubled many workers' pay to five dollars a day in 1914.

claims.text: In 1926 the Ford Motor Company introduced a five-day, 40-hour week for its factory workers.
General Motors, Fiat and Renault did not introduce a five-day, 40-hour week for their factory workers in 1926.
Henry Ford argued that more leisure time would lead workers to buy and use more goods, including cars.
In 1914 Ford raised pay for many of its workers to five dollars a day, roughly double the usual wage.
